seoTitle: Fix Instagram's "Ineligible Country or Region" Error
metaDescription: Fix the Instagram "Ineligible Country or Region" error blocking Boost Post, ads, or monetization by checking your account and ad settings.
intro: The "Ineligible Country or Region" error can block features like Boost Post, ads, or monetization, and it's one of the more frustrating Instagram errors because the message itself gives almost no detail about what's actually wrong. It's commonly caused by region restrictions, incorrect account settings, or a mismatched Facebook ad account connection rather than an outright ban, which means most cases are fixable without contacting support. This guide walks through the checks worth running in order, from your account's basic region setting through to the Facebook Page and Ads connection behind it.

steps.heading: Understand what actually triggers this error
steps.body: Instagram ties monetization and advertising features to a region on file, and that region has to agree across several places at once: your Instagram professional account settings, the Facebook Page linked to it, and the Ads Manager account behind any boosted posts. When any of those disagree, or when a business detail like a payment method or address doesn't match the country you're trying to advertise from, Instagram tends to surface this generic ineligibility message rather than pointing at the specific mismatch. Knowing that it's usually a mismatch, not a ban, changes how you troubleshoot it.

steps.heading: Confirm your Instagram account is set to Professional
steps.body: Boost Post, ads, and most monetization tools only work on Professional accounts, whether Business or Creator, so start by confirming your account is actually set up that way rather than a personal account. If you recently switched account types, region and eligibility settings don't always carry over cleanly, and re-confirming your business category and contact details after a switch can resolve the error on its own.

steps.heading: Check your account's region setting
steps.body: Inside your professional account settings, look for where your business or account location is set and confirm it matches the country you're actually operating and advertising from. A region set incorrectly — sometimes left over from an earlier account setup, a VPN session, or a login from a different country — is one of the most common root causes of this specific error, and it's the first thing worth ruling out before touching anything on the Facebook side.

steps.heading: Reconnect the correct Facebook Page and Ad Account
steps.body: Boosting a post or running ads from Instagram routes through a linked Facebook Page and an Ads Manager account behind it, and if that Page is linked to the wrong Ad Account, or the Ad Account's country doesn't match your Instagram account's region, you'll hit this error even though everything on Instagram itself looks fine. Go into your linked accounts settings, unlink the mismatched Page or Ad Account if needed, and reconnect the correct one so both sides agree on the same country.

steps.heading: Review payment and business details
steps.body: Ads Manager checks your payment method's billing country against the ad account's region, so a card registered to a different country than the one selected for your business can trigger the same ineligibility message even when your Instagram settings are correct. Open your payment settings in Ads Manager and confirm the billing address on file matches the country your account is configured for, updating either the payment method or the account region so they're consistent.

steps.heading: Refresh the app and recheck
steps.body: Once you've corrected a mismatch, changes don't always reflect immediately inside the Instagram app, since it can cache account and eligibility data locally. Force-close and reopen the app, or log out and back in, before trying Boost Post or the ads flow again — trying immediately after a settings change is a common reason people assume a fix didn't work when it just hadn't refreshed yet.

steps.heading: Know when it's a policy issue instead of a settings issue
steps.body: If every setting checks out — matching region, correctly linked Page and Ad Account, and consistent payment details — and the error persists, it may reflect an actual policy restriction on advertising or monetization in your specific country rather than something fixable through account settings. In that case, checking Meta's current list of supported countries for the feature you're trying to use (ads, in-stream monetization, or Stars, for example) will tell you whether you're dealing with a temporary account issue or a hard regional limitation.

faq.question: What causes the Ineligible Country or Region error on Instagram?
faq.answer: It's usually caused by region restrictions, incorrect account settings, or a mismatch between your Instagram account's region and the linked Facebook Page, Ad Account, or payment billing country.

faq.question: Can I fix this myself, or is it always a policy restriction?
faq.answer: Many cases are fixable by correcting your account region, reconnecting your Facebook Page and Ad Account, or updating payment details, though some restrictions on ads or monetization are genuinely policy-based per country.

faq.question: Does this error affect monetization too?
faq.answer: Yes, it can block Boost Post, ads, and monetization features like in-stream ads or Stars depending on your account and region settings.

faq.question: What should I check first if I see this error?
faq.answer: Start by confirming your account is set to Professional and reviewing its region setting, then check that your linked Facebook Page and Ad Account use the same country.

faq.question: Why does the fix not work right after I change my settings?
faq.answer: Instagram can cache account and eligibility data locally, so force-closing and reopening the app, or logging out and back in, is often necessary before a settings change takes effect.
